Hypocrisy

/hih-PAH-kruh-see/ — stress on second syllable · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Hypocrisy is the act of claiming to hold certain beliefs or standards while actually behaving in a way that contradicts them.

It was pure hypocrisy for the litterer to lecture us about keeping the park clean.

Worked Example

The principal who constantly spoke about respect and kindness was caught mocking a struggling student in the hallway.

Hypocrisy is more precise than simply 'dishonesty' because it specifically names the contradiction between claimed beliefs and actual behavior—he preached values he didn't follow. A plain lie might hide the gap; hypocrisy puts it on display.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

deception: deliberately making someone believe something false

insincerity: saying things you do not truly mean

phoniness: a fake, put-on manner or personality

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

integrity: honestly living by the values you claim

sincerity: genuinely meaning what you say and do

Where it sits · how deeply trust is broken — dishonesty → insincerity → hypocrisy → betrayal

dishonesty vs. hypocrisy: Dishonesty is weaker than hypocrisy; dishonesty is any failure to tell the truth, while hypocrisy adds the sting of preaching standards you secretly break.

insincerity vs. hypocrisy: Insincerity is weaker than hypocrisy: insincerity means your words don't match your feelings, but hypocrisy goes further, publicly demanding virtues you refuse to practice yourself.

betrayal vs. hypocrisy: Betrayal is stronger than hypocrisy — hypocrisy breaks faith with your own stated values, while betrayal breaks faith with a person who trusted you, cutting far deeper.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — hypo-

Prefix — hypo-: under (Greek)

Root — cris

Root — cris: to sift, judge, decide (from Greek krinein; the root also shows up as crit-, as in critic)

Suffix — -y

Suffix — -y: state or quality of (noun-forming) (Greek -ia, via Latin and French)

Put it together

Put it together: Hypo- ('under') + cris ('to judge or decide,' from Greek krinein) + -y ('state of'): in ancient Greek, hypokrisis meant answering a fellow actor — playing a part on stage. Hypocrisy is exactly that: performing beliefs on the surface while your real behavior, hidden under the mask, contradicts them.

Use the root in a new word: critic

Use the root in a new word: critic: A film critic's whole job is to judge movies — the same Greek root meaning 'to judge or decide' that hides inside hypocrisy.

Word Choice

formal / literary

Hypocrisy is a serious word for a serious moral flaw—the contradiction between publicly claiming standards and secretly violating them. Reach for it when you want to name this specific gap between preached values and actual behavior. For simple dishonesty or lies, 'deception' or 'lie' works better.
